reading: Every object shifts one cell left (cells pushed off the left edge are lost), then all background cells become 5.
why: output = input translated by (0,-1) with 0 replaced by 5 on every pair

reading: Horizontal coloured lines cross one vertical 8 line. Each other row takes the colour of its nearest horizontal line (a row equidistant from two different colours becomes all 1); line rows become 1 with 8 at the crossing, and the vertical line becomes 1 elsewhere.

slots.lines: full rows containing a 1 at the crossing; their non-1 colour is the band colour
slots.band colour: colour of the nearest line row; tie between different colours -> whole row 1

why: each row is a function of its distance to the line rows
invariants: position of the vertical line column

reading: Two colours each appear as copies of one small shape; every copy of colour A is replaced by colour B's shape (at the same bounding-box top-left) and vice versa.

slots.objects: 8-connected single-colour objects, two colours, one shape per colour
slots.replacement: the other colour's shape, placed at the object's bbox top-left

why: each object position now holds the other colour's shape in the other colour

reading: Isolated single cells move by an offset fixed by their colour: 7 up 2, 2 left 2, 9 down 2, 1 right 1.
why: each marker reappears at its colour's offset; nothing else changes

reading: Each 1 cell sitting on top of a 5 stem drops two rows to the bottom row, replacing the 5 there; its old place becomes 0.

slots.subject: the colour-1 cells
slots.target: constant offset (+2,0), i.e. onto the bottom border row

why: the 1 cells keep their columns and land on the bottom row

reading: In a noisy grid, colour-2 cells form clusters (cells within 2 of each other); every non-2 cell inside each cluster's bounding box becomes 4.

new_rows.name: box2
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, 2).
nb(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- two(Y, X), two(Y2, X2), DY = Y2 - Y, DX = X2 - X, DY >= -2, DY <= 2, DX >= -2, DX <= 2.
reach(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- nb(Y, X, Y2, X2).
reach(Y, X, Y3, X3) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), nb(Y2, X2, Y3, X3).
lab(Y, X, min(K)) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), K = Y2 * 100 + X2.
top(K, min(Y)) :- lab(Y, X, K).
bot(K, max(Y)) :- lab(Y, X, K).
lft(K, min(X)) :- lab(Y, X, K).
rgt(K, max(X)) :- lab(Y, X, K).
box2(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !two(Y, X), top(K, T), bot(K, B), lft(K, L), rgt(K, R), Y >= T, Y <= B, X >= L, X <= R.

why: exactly the non-2 cells inside the 2-cluster bounding boxes change, all to 4

reading: Vertical bars of 8 and 2 stand on the bottom row; a new 5 bar is drawn two columns right of the last bar, bottom-aligned, with height = (number of 8 cells) - (number of 2 cells).
why: the only change is a bottom-aligned 5 run of that height in that column

reading: A two-colour pattern grows one layer: every background cell that touches the pattern diagonally but not orthogonally is painted with the pattern's inner colour (the colour not on its bounding-box edge).

new_rows.name: halo
new_rows.datalog:
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
dfg(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), off(DY, DX), off(DY, 0), off(0, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
ofg(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y, X2, C).
ofg(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, cell(Y2, X, C).
halo(Y, X) :- dfg(Y, X), !ofg(Y, X).

slots.colour: the inner fg colour (fg colour absent from the fg bounding-box edge); varies per pair, so not train/own

why: exactly the halo cells change, all to the inner colour

reading: A rectangular frame encloses an inner block of another colour; a ring of the inner colour is added around the frame, its thickness = the inner block's smaller side, reduced to the smallest margin to the grid edge.

slots.shape: the one framed object (outer colour on its bbox edge)
slots.thickness: min(inner height, inner width, margins to all four grid edges)
slots.region: background cells within that distance (Chebyshev) of the shape's bbox

why: exactly the background cells in the square ring around the bbox change, to the inner colour

reading: Each 3-cell L of 8 fills the missing corner of its 2x2 box with 1.

new_rows.name: lcorner
new_rows.datalog: lcorner(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C0), !cell(Y, X, C0), off(DY, DX), off(DY, 0), off(0, DX), Y1 = Y + DY, X1 = X + DX, cell(Y1, X, A), cell(Y, X1, B), cell(Y1, X1, D).

why: exactly the background cell completing each 2x2 L becomes 1
